text:
Priya: Anyone else seeing dashboard slowness in eu-canary? multiple customer pings about sparkline frame drops and long initial paint. noticed after last canary deploy.
Miguel: Yep, metrics look bad — average chart LCP jumped 640ms -> ~1.4s for canary users. flamegraph points to a big parse/import step in telemetry client.
Tom: When did the telemetry change land? @DeployBot can you paste the recent canary deploys?
DeployBot: deploy: canary/eu rollout 2024-10-12T13:45Z by Tom — service: console-client, tag: telemetry-sampler-v2.
Ava: That was me — I bumped sampling for canary from 1% -> 10% to collect more traces. I didn't expect it to pull in the analytics helper (and its polyfills). my bad.
Miguel: Confirming - build artifacts show a huge telemetry chunk now.
Miguel: ```
$ ls -lh dist/static/js | egrep "telemetry|chart"
-rw-r--r-- 1 build 2.6M telemetry.chunk.js
-rw-r--r-- 1 build 512K chart.chunk.js
```
Miguel: telemetry.chunk.js contains a 3rd-party analytics lib and a small polyfill that gets eagerly imported at app bootstrap.
Ava: So front-end parse + polyfills increasing main-thread work. Sara: also seeing backend hotspots — routing weight tweak earlier today pushed more dashboard traffic to a dedicate pool that has lower KV-prefetch affinity. kvcache hit rate dropped.
Sara: kvcache_hit_rate: 0.56 -> 0.12 around 13:48Z (matches deploy). backend p95 latency for tiles rose 60ms -> 220ms.
Priya: So two compounding problems: 1) client bundle bloat causing parse/LCP regression, 2) routing/quota change causing KV-prefetch misses -> higher backend latency — both amplify UX regressions.
Tom: Quick mitigation options: rollback sampler flag in infra for canary, and a tiny client patch to lazy-load telemetry so it doesn't block bootstrap. I can open PR for the lazy-import.
Miguel: Lazy-import pattern suggestion:
Miguel: ```js
useEffect(() => {
  if (shouldInitTelemetry()) {
    import('lib/telemetry').then(t => t.init({sample: 0.1}));
  }
}, []);
```
Tom: That should keep the heavy chunk out of the initial parse.
Ava: I'll flip the sampler flag back to 1% for canary now. will post infra change.
DeployBot: rollback: canary/eu telemetry-sampler-v2 rollback triggered by Ava at 2024-10-12T14:01Z.
Miguel: Rebuilt a local artifact with telemetry lazy-imported — sizes:
Miguel: ```
before: telemetry.chunk.js 2.6MB
after: telemetry.lazy.chunk.js 390KB
```
Miguel: Early local perf run shows main-thread parse drop back to ~700ms. not perfect but much better.
Sara: I'll also revert the routing-weight tweak on the platform side — pushing traffic back to nodes with better prefetch affinity. moving weight from 1.2 -> 0.85 now.
Priya: Nice. Action summary: Ava rolls back sampler, Tom lands lazy-import PR to staging, Sara reverts routing weight, Miguel validates build size. Watch canary for 30–60m and report if frame drops persist.
Tom: PR opened: #4228 lazy-import-telemetry (small). cc @Priya @Miguel
Ava: rollback done and infra rollout started.
DeployBot: canary/eu deploy: routing-weight-revert by Sara at 2024-10-12T14:08Z.
Miguel: Confirming telemetry chunk size reduced on next canary build artifact.
Priya: Great coordination — keep an eye on observability; if p95 doesn't normalize in 30m we revert the canary and start a deeper dive. :thumbsup:
Tom: :rocket:
Ava: :thumbsup:
Sara: monitoring kvcache_hit_rate and p95, will ping here if anything odd.
Miguel: will run a couple quick UX traces after the next canary build.
Priya: closing for now, reopen if any customer regressions show up.
